intent: Single-variable step from the iteration 8 design: sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016 m, the largest allowed footprint. The aim is to cut line-loss events, which are about 1 per run and cost up to about 15 points, by keeping the sum of sensor readings above the 0.05 line-loss threshold on bend entries. All other geometry is unchanged, so the Integrator's controller and the iteration 8 result remain directly comparable. Expect line_loss_events to fall toward 0.5, with rms_error and completions held at about 0.01 m and 60/60.
learning: Iteration 8 showed that wheel_track 0.11 to 0.105 m completed all 60 slalom, s-bend and oval trials, so yaw authority is no longer the limit. Next iteration, check: (a) whether line_loss_events fall below 0.85 on the slalom and s-bend, which would confirm that sensor footprint is causing the dropouts; (b) whether rms_error rises above 0.01 m, which would mean the wider footprint blurs the signal on the sharpest bends; (c) whether completion_time holds near 2.2 s on the slalom; (d) whether any run goes off track. Ask the Integrator whether the signal is smoother with the wider footprint and whether kd or kp needs retuning.
rationale: Iteration 8 is the best design so far (score 939.3). All 60 development trials finished on oval, s-bend and slalom, with progress of about 0.996 to 0.998. The score now comes mainly from three terms: line_loss_events (about 0.85 to 1.05 per run, worth up to 15 points), completion_time (about 1.9 to 2.3 s, worth about 16 points at 2.2 s), and rms_error (about 0.006 to 0.010 m, worth about 65 points). Agility has been the lever since iteration 3, and wheel_track was the last step with a clear gain. Further yaw-inertia cuts are at their limits: body_length 0.10 m, mass 0.40 kg, body_width 0.08 m (off-track floor unchanged). The remaining evidence points at line loss rather than yaw response. Line loss occurs about once per run even though the robot finishes, which suggests brief dropouts when the outer sensors lose the 12 mm footprint on the 25 mm tape during bend entries. A larger sensor footprint should keep the sum of readings above the 0.05 threshold and smooth the signal. The change is a single variable: sensor_size goes from 0.012 to 0.016 m, the largest allowed value, and everything else stays as in iteration 8 so the Integrator's controller carries over and the effect is attributable. Expected result: line_loss_events fall from about 1 toward 0.5 or below, rms_error stays near or below 0.01 m, and completions hold at 60/60. Risk: a wider footprint blurs the signal on the sharpest bends and raises rms_error or steering_oscillation. If that happens, I will return to 0.012 m and look at wheel_radius for speed instead.
